literal: An edict said: "The five teachings govern the pivot; since antiquity choosing for it has been hard. Unless one is kin, worthy, and urgently needed, none should answer this call."
idiomatic: An edict read: "The five teachings sit at the heart of rule, and since antiquity the right choice has been rare. Only kin who are also worthy and urgently needed should take up this charge."

literal: The King, with bright virtue and earnest kinship, was entrusted as guardian and tutor; going out he guarded the border marches, coming in he wore the grand regalia—inward and outward in harmony, people and spirits alike attached to him.
idiomatic: The king's bright virtue and close kinship made him guardian and tutor; abroad he held the frontier, at court he wore the grand robes—within and without in harmony, and people and spirits alike looked to him.

literal: Now, leading the army's banner, his awesomeness and title should weigh heavy; he may again be granted Minister over the Masses to brighten his repute and substance.
idiomatic: Now that he led the army, his prestige deserved weight; he was again made Minister over the Masses to magnify his standing.

literal: An edict also made Xie, in his present office, concurrently Inspector of Yang Province.
idiomatic: Another edict kept his present offices and added inspector of Yang Province.

literal: Xie simplified punishments and guided ritual; he rested the people. Within the province there was no trouble; far and near were quiet.
idiomatic: Xie eased punishments, guided ritual, and let the people rest; the province was untroubled and far and near were calm.

literal: Within Yang Province's jurisdiction, the Jian'an garrison commander Hu Jinglue still held out for Baojuan and would not submit; Xie attacked by land and water, and Jinglue came out bound in person to surrender.
idiomatic: Jian'an garrison commander Hu Jinglue still held for Baojuan; Xie attacked by land and water until Jinglue came out bound to surrender.

literal: From Xie's arrival at Shouchun, he pacified eastern garrisons and towns as far as Yangshi; in the west Jian'an submitted; mountain tribes obeyed; heads taken and captives numbered in the tens of thousands.
idiomatic: From Shouchun he secured the east to Yangshi, took Jian'an in the west, won the mountain tribes, and counted tens of thousands in heads and captives.

literal: He was advanced to Grand Marshal and continued as Minister over the Masses; the rest was as before.
idiomatic: He was promoted to grand marshal while keeping the ministry; all else unchanged.

literal: His fief was increased by eight hundred households.
idiomatic: His fief grew by eight hundred households.

literal: Again Baojuan sent the general Chen Bozhi to camp at Feikou, and Hu Song held Liang city; the water army stretched in succession for more than two hundred li.
idiomatic: Baojuan again sent Chen Bozhi to Feikou and Hu Song to Liang city, with a water line over two hundred li.

literal: Xie disposed his officers and men to attack the camps separately; Bozhi and Hu Song led their masses out to fight; the generals struck them and took nine thousand heads and ten thousand captives.
idiomatic: Xie split his forces against the camps; Bozhi and Hu Song came out and were beaten—nine thousand heads and ten thousand prisoners.

literal: Bozhi and the others barely escaped with their lives and camped at Fenghuo.
idiomatic: Bozhi and the rest barely escaped and camped at Fenghuo.

literal: Xie again ordered the generals to fight repeatedly; Bozhi's plans were exhausted and he fled by night.
idiomatic: Xie ordered repeated attacks until Bozhi's plans failed and he fled by night.

literal: The Huainan region was pacified. An edict said: "The King, as kin, honors the highest minister; in merit and virtue he has no second. My heart is dim in knowledge; in instruction and guardianship I rely on him."
idiomatic: Huainan was pacified. An edict said: "As kin you honor the highest minister; in merit none stands beside you. My judgment is dim—I lean on you for counsel and guard."

literal: Lately, when Shouchun was first opened, the duty of suppression was weighty; therefore the King was ordered personally to direct the main army and pacify the far Huai.
idiomatic: When Shouchun first fell the burden of holding it was heavy, so you were sent in person to command the host and pacify the Huai frontier.

literal: Braving this scorching heat, with canopy and carriage swaying in the wind, prolonged campaigning over time must bring loss and harm.
idiomatic: You braved this heat with canopy and carriage in the wind; long campaigning must wear you down.

literal: Long kept from audience, day and night my feelings are bound to you.
idiomatic: Kept from audience so long, day and night my heart is bound to you.

literal: Moreover your victories and plans were proclaimed together, awe and effect both manifest; public and private alike approved—righteousness demands admiration.
idiomatic: Your victories and plans together showed their power; public and private alike praised what duty required us to honor.

literal: Though triumph has a set day, I cannot defer my longing; Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gate Zheng Daozhao may go there to pay respects on my behalf."
idiomatic: Though your return is fixed, I cannot wait to see you—send Palace Attendant Zheng Daozhao to greet you there."

literal: Xie was summoned back to court.
idiomatic: Xie was recalled to court.

literal: Xie's government honored leniency; he did not violate the slightest thing. The gentry and commoners of Huainan pursued his remaining kindness and still think of him.
idiomatic: Xie ruled with leniency and touched nothing unjust; Huainan's people still cherish what he left them.

literal: At first, when Xie pacified Shouchun, he captured Xiao Baojuan's Administrator of Ruyin Wang Guo, Yu Province aide Yu Ji, and several others; Xie opened his breast in courtesy to them and often had them share his seat.
idiomatic: When he took Shouchun he captured Baojuan's Ruyin administrator Wang Guo, Yu Province aide Yu Ji, and others; Xie treated them with open courtesy and often seated them beside him.

literal: Guo seized an interval to advance and said: "Guo and the others have been torn from their lives' bond; white hair is scattered abroad; looking west at the setting sun, how little light remains."
idiomatic: Guo spoke up: "We have been torn from our life's bond; white hair is scattered abroad; looking west at the setting sun, how little light remains."

literal: "Now we meet sage transformation and ought to exert what strength these foolish old men have and show our measure—but south of the river we have a hundred mouths, life and death divided; we beg to return beyond the river and declare your virtuous grace."
idiomatic: "Now under your sage rule we should exert what these old men still have—but south of the river a hundred mouths stand divided between life and death; let us return beyond the river and declare your grace."

literal: Xie pitied them and granted it.
idiomatic: Xie pitied them and agreed.

literal: Guo thanked him again, saying: "Your Highness's treatment of us has surpassed a state's scholar."
idiomatic: Guo thanked him again: "Your Highness has treated us beyond what a state's scholar deserves."

literal: "Guo and the others now return, bearing your kind grace on our backs; we ask leave for your benevolent carriage to shake the army and turn our tracks beyond the river."
idiomatic: "We go home carrying your kindness on our backs; grant your carriage to shake the host so we may turn our steps beyond the river."

literal: Only then did they return.
idiomatic: Only then did they return.

literal: Such was how the distant held him in their hearts.
idiomatic: So deeply did distant peoples hold him in their hearts.

literal: When Xie reached the capital, Shizong received him at the Eastern Hall and addressed Xie: "Lately the phoenix has not come,[2] the dark masses are in two transformations—therefore I bent your honored counsel to soothe and cherish the border adherents; yet the bandit chieftain was benighted and dared fight in Huai-Chu."
idiomatic: At the capital Shizong received him in the Eastern Hall and said: "The phoenix has not yet come,[2] the people stand between two orders—so I bent your counsel to win the frontier; yet that benighted bandit dared fight in Huai-Chu."

literal: "Uncle's heroic strategy is lofty and bright; responding to the moment you extinguished and settled them; triumph this day—prostrate, I ease my sorrowful waiting."
idiomatic: "Uncle, your strategy is bright; you answered the moment and ended them. Today's triumph eases what I have long grieved and waited for."

literal: Xie thanked him, saying: "Your servant disgracefully fills the post of frontier commander, pacifying the new and the old, yet could not spread martial power and guide grace, aweing and cherishing far and near."
idiomatic: Xie replied: "I disgracefully held the frontier and could not spread force and grace to awe far and near."

literal: "This caused the petty chieftain Bozhi to drive ant-like followers and harass the border forts."
idiomatic: "That let the petty Bozhi drive ant-like followers against our border forts."

literal: "Not only do I look up ashamed before Heaven's face; in truth I also bow my head ashamed before the court ranks."
idiomatic: "I am ashamed before your face and before the court alike."

literal: "The Spring and Autumn Annals blame the commander; your servant truly bears it."
idiomatic: "Spring and Autumn blames the commander—and that blame is mine."

literal: "Relying on Your Majesty's deep mercy in setting aside faults, therefore this foolish servant escaped punishment."
idiomatic: "Only your deep mercy let this fool escape punishment."

literal: Xie repeatedly memorialized to resign Grand Marshal, concurrent Minister over the Masses, and the added fief, begging to return to Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Xie repeatedly asked to resign grand marshal, the ministry, and the added fief and return to Zhongshan.

literal: An edict did not permit it.
idiomatic: The throne refused.

literal: He was then made Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant; Minister over the Masses as before.
idiomatic: He was made recorder of the Masters of Writing and palace attendant while keeping the ministry.

literal: He firmly refused but could not escape.
idiomatic: He refused firmly but could not escape office.

literal: Xie by nature loved quiet simplicity and did not let power and profit touch his heart.
idiomatic: Xie loved quiet simplicity and let power and profit never touch his heart.

literal: Gaozu valued his capacity for affairs and would not release him.
idiomatic: Gaozu valued his capacity and would not release him.

literal: Though at the verge of death the testament again had Shizong detain him; each time it went against his wish.
idiomatic: Even the deathbed testament had Shizong keep him—each time against his wish.

literal: He often sighed in sorrow; because the edict's words were earnest, he bent his will and answered the charge.
idiomatic: He often sighed; when the edict pressed earnestly he bent his will and obeyed.

literal: At that time Prince Xi of Xianyang grew daily proud and had many unlawful acts; Prince Xiang of Beihai spoke of it privately to Shizong, and Shizong deeply resented it.
idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang grew proud and lawless; Prince Xiang of Beihai spoke privately to Shizong, who came to resent him deeply.

literal: He also said Xie had won great popular feeling and ought not long remain chief minister, urging Shizong to follow Gaozu's testament charge.
idiomatic: He also said Xie had won the people's hearts and should not long stay chief minister, urging Shizong to follow Gaozu's testament.

literal: Xi and the others also sent out the commander of the army Yu Lie as Hengzhou inspector—not Lie's wish; they forced him firmly, and Lie deeply resented it.
idiomatic: Xi and the others also sent army commander Yu Lie to Hengzhou—not his wish; they forced him, and he burned with resentment.

literal: Lie's son Zhong had once been at the emperor's side; he secretly ordered Zhong to tell Shizong: "The princes' intentions cannot be measured; they should be removed and Your Majesty should early take government into his own view."
idiomatic: Lie's son Zhong, once at court, was told in secret: "The princes' minds cannot be read—remove them and take the reins early."

literal: At that time the autumn di sacrifice was due; the princes and dukes all fasted in the temple's eastern lodge.
idiomatic: The autumn di sacrifice was due; princes and dukes fasted in the temple's eastern lodge.

literal: Shizong sent Yu Lie with more than sixty stalwart night guards to summon Xi, Xie, Xiang, and the others, bring them in, and receive them at the Hall of Ultimate Light.
idiomatic: Shizong sent Yu Lie with sixty-odd night guards to summon Xi, Xie, Xiang, and the rest to the Hall of Ultimate Light.

literal: Shizong said to Xie: "Lately north-south affairs have been pressing; I could not honor your lofty withdrawal."
idiomatic: Shizong told Xie: "North and south have pressed me—I could not honor your wish to withdraw."

literal: "What sort of man is Ke that he dares long defy the former charge? Now I follow uncle's intent to tread the high path."
idiomatic: "What is Ke that he should defy the former charge? Now I grant uncle's wish to walk the high path."

literal: Xie thanked him, saying: "The late emperor, not deeming your servant shallow and slight, bent down the grace of not forgetting me; in and out we were bound close, public and private without reserve."
idiomatic: Xie replied: "The late emperor, not deeming me slight, bent down grace that never forgot me; in and out we were bound, public and private without reserve."

literal: "Since Your Majesty's dragon flew to the ninety-fifth degree, I have repeatedly sought release; the chief ministers suppressed it, and Your Majesty also would not grant it."
idiomatic: "Since Your Majesty took the throne I have sought release again and again—the ministers blocked it and you would not grant it."

literal: "In midsummer of the year before last I again dusted Heaven's hearing; then I was graciously lent out as Dingzhou inspector."
idiomatic: "Midsummer before last I troubled Heaven's ear again and was lent out as Dingzhou inspector."

literal: "The year before I returned to Luoyang and was ordered to command the Huai-Fei armies; though without merit I barely escaped guilt."
idiomatic: "The year before I returned to Luoyang and was ordered to command Huai-Fei; though I achieved little I barely escaped blame."

literal: "Hardly had I returned when I was again entrusted with a post beyond my measure."
idiomatic: "Hardly home, I was again given a post beyond my measure."

literal: "Your servant has repeatedly troubled requests, all set out plainly to the sage ear."
idiomatic: "I have troubled you with requests, all plainly set before your ear."

literal: "Your Majesty's filial depth is without change; looking up you follow the former edict, above completing the beauty of sagely clarity, below fulfilling this petty servant's wish—moved by present and past, joy and sorrow interweave."
idiomatic: "Your filial heart is unchanged; you follow the former edict above, complete sagely clarity, and below fulfill my wish—past and present move me, joy and sorrow together."

literal: An edict then said: "The King from old has honored quiet; his will abandons worldly affairs. The late emperor loved and brightened this to the utmost and would not seize that feeling; the testament is clear and permits this lofty withdrawal."
idiomatic: An edict said: "The king has long honored quiet and abandoned worldly affairs. The late emperor loved that brightness and would not seize it; the testament clearly permits this withdrawal."

literal: "His refined conduct does not shift; I too have not dared to violate and seize it."
idiomatic: "His refined conduct does not shift; I too have not dared to seize it."

literal: "Now he releases office and returns to his residence; hill and garden are his to tend—lofty conduct, firm and true; the integrity of Ben and Lü, far to pursue."
idiomatic: "Now he leaves office for his residence and tends hill and garden—conduct lofty and firm, the integrity of Ben and Lü, hard to follow."

literal: "Yet the king's house is newly built and funds and strength are much lacking; the term of completion, by months, is not reached."
idiomatic: "Yet his house is newly built and funds are short; completion is still months away."

literal: "Measure and send laborers, distribute timber and tile according to the king's liking, quickly have it made—strive for simplicity to match the king's heart."
idiomatic: "Send measured labor and timber and tile as he wishes, build quickly and simply to match his heart."

literal: Xie thereupon composed the "Fly" rhapsody to express his feelings, hating slander and framing.
idiomatic: Xie then wrote the "Fly" rhapsody to voice his feelings, hating slander and plots.

literal: Again Xie was made Grand Preceptor; Xie then firmly refused.
idiomatic: He was again made grand preceptor; Xie refused firmly.

literal: An edict said: "The two principles divide their images; the positions of ruler and minister take form."
idiomatic: An edict said: "Heaven and earth divide their signs and ruler and minister take their places."

literal: Once upper and lower have their places, the meaning of leading and following arises.
idiomatic: Once ranks are set, leading and following arise.

literal: Since antiquity, lords who hold Heaven's position—how have they not relied on bright teachers and leaned on worthy assistants, and only afterward harmonized yin and yang and ordered the people's constant norms?
idiomatic: Since antiquity, who has held Heaven's seat without bright teachers and worthy assistants before harmonizing yin and yang and ordering the people's norms?

literal: Those who go and do not return—the ancients truly had them; this is what is called keeping goodness for oneself alone while disordering the great norms, the men of mountains and forests.
idiomatic: Those who go and never return—the ancients knew them too; they kept goodness alone and broke the great norms, men of mountain and forest.

literal: Worthy men and noble sons are not so.
idiomatic: Worthy men and noble sons are not like that.

literal: They bend themselves to settle the people, strain their persons to aid things—what is called using prior knowledge to awaken later knowledge, sharing dust and cleansing the world together.
idiomatic: They bend themselves to settle the people and strain their persons to aid the world—awakening the late with the early, sharing dust until all are clean.

literal: "I, coarse in tender years, have inherited the precious succession and truly rely on uncle's power to rescue; it is right that he forever hold both general and minister to weave inner and outer."
idiomatic: "Young and coarse on the throne, I truly rely on uncle's rescue; he should forever hold general and minister to weave within and without."

literal: "Yet forced to seize the former charge, I fear violating lofty withdrawal; I bend my will and cut my heart to follow high simplicity."
idiomatic: "Yet forced to seize the former charge I feared violating his withdrawal; I bent my will and cut my heart to follow his simplicity."

literal: "Lately because flood and drought are out of harmony and yin and yang lose order, I therefore bend the king to discuss the Way, hoping to harmonize this jade candle."
idiomatic: "Lately flood and drought and yin and yang have fallen out of step—so I bend the king to discuss the Way and harmonize the jade candle of rule."

literal: "Moreover the teacher-minister may be at ease without abandoning pure elevation—thus the Duke of Zhou returned the government and dwelt in it; the Martial Father ended his post at a full century."
idiomatic: "A teacher-minister may be at ease without losing pure elevation—the Duke of Zhou returned rule yet remained; the Martial Father ended at a full age."

literal: "The king's righteousness embraces family and state; principle forbids standing alone on high—a palace attendant may go to instruct him earnestly."
idiomatic: "The king's duty embraces family and state; principle forbids standing alone on high—send a palace attendant to instruct him earnestly."

literal: Shizong also wrote a family letter to Xie: "Ke says: receiving your returned report, you still hold lofty modesty. Ke is truly dim and few; in government craft there is much chaff; the trust of support and correction relies on honored kin."
idiomatic: Shizong also wrote him as family: "Ke says: your report still holds lofty modesty. Ke is dim and few; government has much chaff; support and correction rely on you."

literal: "Father's virtue and repute are both weighty; teacherly instruction is where we return—how can we near abandon family and state and far honor pure elevation?"
idiomatic: "Father's virtue and repute are weighty; teacherly instruction is our return—how can we nearly abandon family and state for distant purity?"

literal: "I only wish you would bend down in time to match the heart that leans on you."
idiomatic: "Only bend down in time to match the heart that leans on you."

literal: Xie had no way out and answered the charge.
idiomatic: Xie had no way out and obeyed.

literal: Afterward Shizong repeatedly visited Xie's residence.
idiomatic: Afterward Shizong often visited his house.

literal: When the Jingzhao and Guangping princes were violent and unlawful, an edict ordered the night-guard squad chief to lead feathered forest tiger guards and confine the princes at their residences.
idiomatic: When the Jingzhao and Guangping princes turned violent, an edict had the night-guard chief lead tiger guards to confine the princes in their houses.

literal: Xie submitted a memorial urgently remonstrating; Shizong did not accept it.
idiomatic: Xie memorialized urgently; Shizong would not hear it.

literal: Xie, having neither the pleasure of mountains and waters nor the company of knowing friends, faced only wife and children and was depressed and unhappy.
idiomatic: Without mountains, waters, or knowing friends, he faced only wife and children and grew depressed.

literal: When deliberating on statutes and ordinances, Xie together with Prince Yong of Gaoyang, the Eight Seats, and court scholars of talent met every five days to discuss whether the rules and measures were fitting.
idiomatic: When statutes were debated, Xie met every five days with Prince Yong of Gaoyang, the Eight Seats, and learned courtiers to weigh what fit.

literal: Moreover Xie from old attended Gaozu and was moreover penetrating and broad in hearing; in whatever he decided, the men of the age looked up to him.
idiomatic: He had long attended Gaozu and was penetrating and broad in hearing; whatever he decided, men of the age looked up.

literal: Added to this were fine looks and good bearing; stern as a spirit, turning and advancing in proper measure; in going out, speech, and laughter, viewers forgot fatigue.
idiomatic: Fine looks and bearing, stern as a spirit, every turn measured—in speech and laughter watchers forgot fatigue.

literal: He was again made Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: He was again made palace attendant.

literal: Xie honored literature and history; in the intervals of affairs he unceasingly read.
idiomatic: Xie honored literature and history and read without cease between affairs.

literal: He compiled from ancient emperors, kings, and worthies down to Wei imperial sons and grandsons, thirty scrolls, titled Essentials in Brief.
idiomatic: He compiled thirty scrolls from ancient rulers and worthies down to Wei imperial kin, titled Essentials in Brief.

literal: Careful and cautious, at first he had no faults; even in leisure and feasting he had no slack color or lazy bearing.
idiomatic: Careful from the first, he had no faults; even at leisure he showed no slackness.

literal: He loved and respected Confucian talents and bent his heart to courtesy toward them.
idiomatic: He loved Confucian talent and bent his heart to courtesy.

literal: Upright, pure, and frugal; his gate had no private callers.
idiomatic: Upright, pure, and frugal—his gate knew no private callers.

literal: By nature he was benevolent and filial; speaking at court, he had his maternal uncle Pan Senggu made Administrator of Leling in Ji Province.
idiomatic: Benevolent and filial by nature, he spoke at court and had his uncle Pan Senggu made Leling administrator in Ji.

literal: [3] Prince Yu of Jingzhao framed rebellion; Senggu was compelled to follow him.
idiomatic: [3] Prince Yu of Jingzhao rebelled; Senggu was forced to follow.

literal: Minister over the Masses Gao Zhao by nature was fierce and obstinate and harmed worthy and outstanding men.
idiomatic: Minister Gao Zhao was fierce by nature and harmed the worthy.

literal: Moreover Zhao's elder brother's daughter entered as consort; when Empress Shun died, Shizong wished to make her empress; Xie firmly held that it could not be done.
idiomatic: Zhao's brother's daughter had entered the inner quarters; when Empress Shun died Shizong wished to make her empress, and Xie firmly refused.

literal: Zhao therefore repeatedly slandered Xie to Shizong; Shizong did not accept it.
idiomatic: Zhao then slandered Xie again and again; Shizong would not hear it.

literal: Because Senggu had shared Yu's rebellion, Zhao slandered that Xie in the north communicated with Yu and in the south recruited barbarian bandits.
idiomatic: When Senggu shared Yu's rebellion, Zhao claimed Xie had conspired with Yu in the north and recruited southern tribes.
